newsitem.title: ITALY: Ex-UK Chancellor welcomes Bank of England freedom.
newsitem.headline: Ex-UK Chancellor welcomes Bank of England freedom.

text.p: Former British Chancellor of the Exchequer Nigel Lawson, who served under former Conservative Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher, welcomed a recent move to give the Bank of England more independence.

Lawson, now a member of Britain's House of Lords, told reporters at a conference on Saturday in this lakeside resort in northern Italy, the new Labour government's move to allow the central bank to set interest rates was "a very good decision."

Lawson, who resigned from being Thatcher's chancellor in October 1989 after a difference over economic policy, said: "I tried to persuade Margaret Thatcher to do that but I was unable to get her to agree."
New Labour Chancellor Gordon Brown last week announced the creation of a monetary policy committee which would set interest rates to meet an inflation target laid down by the government.
Previously the chancellor alone set interest rates after taking advice from the Bank of England.

Brown's move has been welcomed by another former Conservative chancellor Norman Lamont but criticised as "unwise" by Kenneth Clarke, the last Conservative chancellor before the party lost power in a general election on May 1.
